Senses.Explanation: Literally a “good knowing acquaintance,” this corpus-wide person label names a good teacher, guide, or good friend. The term occurs 2,832 times in 311 allowlisted texts. Dahui directly says, “those called good teachers guide all beings and cause them to see nature” (夫稱善知識者，引導一切眾生，令見佛性), then describes observing people's capacities and giving teaching as medicine matches illness. He calls such reception and guidance “the proper work a good teacher ought to do” (善知識本分合做底事), and elsewhere mentions “a good teacher's eye for distinguishing people” (善知識辨人眼). The Five Lamps Compendium describes travelling people “visiting good teachers” (參善知識). Another narrative has a student say, “a great good teacher is hard to encounter even across ages; now that I have met one, why begrudge body or life?” (大善知識歷劫難逢，今既得遇，豈惜身命). Asked “what is a good teacher?” (如何是善知識), Fohai replies that lanterns, pillars, cats, and dogs are all called good teachers. The same label supplies the vocative “Good friends!” when speakers address assemblies. Direct address changes who is being hailed, not the lexical kind of label.
Senses.Note: Dahui's role definition and Fohai's materially different answer are both retained, preventing an exclusively institutional or human-office definition. The former role and vocative targets applied the same label to people in referential and direct-address grammar and are merged. Compare the entries for accomplished person, lineage teacher, visiting a good teacher, general address, and ascending the hall.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫稱善知識者。引導一切眾生。令見佛性。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄). Dahui Zonggao directly defines those called good teachers as guiding beings and causing them to see nature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這箇是善知識本分合做底事。豈是彊為。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄). Dahui Zonggao calls receiving and maturing those who travelled to the gathering 'the proper work a good teacher ought to do,' not something forced.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是善知識。臣云。燈籠露柱猫兒狗子。皆稱善知識何必更問。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Continued Record of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Lingyin Huiyuan's report before the emperor. Lingyin is the exact self-speaker: answering Zeng Kai's question, he says lanterns, pillars, cats, and dogs are all called good teachers and asks why another must be sought.

Occurrences.Kwic: 凡行脚人參善知識。到一叢林。放下瓶鉢。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Baoci Xingyan section. Baoci Xingyan is the exact hall speaker who says that travelling practitioners visit good teachers, reach a monastery, and set down bottle and bowls.

Occurrences.Kwic: 非但失却善知識辨人眼。亦乃賺他百劫千生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄). Dahui Zonggao names 'a good teacher's eye for distinguishing people' while criticizing acceptance of a person's presentation for irrelevant reasons.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！一行三昧者，於一切處行住坐臥，常行一直心是也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Teaching-Treasure Record of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經). Huineng addresses the assembly as 'Good friends!' before defining complete command of the single conduct.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！一言半句實有起死回生之力、翻窠倒臼之施
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huiyue Xu (晦嶽旭禪師語錄). Huiyue Xu hails the assembly as 'Good friends!' in his public address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大善知識歷劫難逢。今既得遇，豈惜身命！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Heze Shenhui section. Shenhui is the exact thinker: while being struck by Huineng, the narrative explicitly introduces the stored words as Shenhui's reflection.
